newsitem.title: JAPAN: Moody's cuts M'bishi Estate long-term debt rating.
newsitem.headline: Moody's cuts M'bishi Estate long-term debt rating.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Wednesday that it had downgraded the long-term debt rating of Mitsubishi Estate Co Ltd to A1 from Aa2.

Moody's said its secured and unsecured long-term debt ratings for the major property developer and its wholly owned finance company, MEC Finance USA Inc, had been lowered to A1 from Aa2, and that its shelf registration rating for Mitsubishi Estate had been also lowered to (P)A1 from (P)Aa2.

The move reflects Moody's view that the continued dismal operating environment, competition from major new projects for "intelligent" buildings, and the cost of upgrading the company's buildings would restrain the recovery of cash flow from its core lease properties in the centre of Tokyo, it said.

Moody's added that the rating also reflects its expectation that the company's lease portfolio in the Marunouchi business district of central Tokyo will remain one of the most valuable property franchises in Japan in view of its premier location and excellent tenant portfolio.
The company's substantial financial cushion in the form of marketable securities will continue to sustain its adequate financial flexibility, it said.
